newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian civil servant pensions need reform - PM.
newsitem.headline: Belgian civil servant pensions need reform - PM.

text.p: Belgian Prime Minister Jean-Luc Dehaene said Sunday the pension system for civil servants had to be reformed.

"We must wonder whether every margin for wage increases for civil servants should be limited by the obligation for similar increases for civil servant pensions," Dehaene told Belgian BRTN radio. "It is necessary to rethink (the civil servant pension system) without completely reshuffling it."
In the Belgian centre-left government's 1997 budget, approved by parliament last week, it was decided to raise the retirement age for women to 65 years from 60 within 13 years.
The budget introduced some austerity measures for private sector pensions but left the civil servant pensions untouched.
Friday, Belgium's socialist civil servant unions called for a national strike in all public services if the government embarks on a reform of their pension system.
One of Dehaene's government's top priorities is the long-awaited reform of Belgium's generous social security system. The reform is expected to be the focus of government policy in coming months.
